My shoes are under your counter. Sorry. I took them off and now I can't face putting them back on.
A client called it Brindle Fever. All I know is I'm shivering, and the clinic opens at dawn.
Any of those plain little medicine bottles left? I've got my own money. Could I sit here while you ring it up?
Two dinners, please. The woman on coat check always says she's eaten. She hasn't.
My mother sang the last verse in Dutch tonight. A man by the door knew every word.
He stayed after the show to tell her he'd forgotten what his mother's voice sounded like. She sang it again.
Got anything soft to eat? I owe my voice a night off.
Someone booked two men under the name James Bailey. Neither wanted the table once Security came in.
I've got one pencil left and I'm writing people's real names in ink from now on.
Tea for the desk, please. Tomorrow's bookings can wait for the kettle.
A client paid me extra to confess something awful. He'd eaten his flatmate's good cheese.
Three hours I kept that secret. Now I'm hungry and apparently you know too.
You have any cheese? Yes, I see the irony.
Last tram went past with the lights off. I could see the driver eating his sandwich.
Part of me wants to complain. The other part wants to know where he got the bread.
Something for the walk home. Nothing that needs a fork.
I've had six men ask who does my braid. One actually sat down and let me show him.
We missed the opening number. He did the last bit himself, though. Got it dead straight.
Dinner for one. I'll take the long way home so the mist doesn't undo my hair.
Someone asked me to sing the song my old partner wrote. Haven't touched it in years.
I made it through the first verse. The pianist hummed the rest with me.
A bottle of water for the pianist too. She saved my neck tonight.
We voted to get a stool for the door shift. Then we held a meeting about where to put the stool.
I stood through both meetings. You'll forgive me if I lean on this counter.
I'm feeding the late shift. Something that splits four ways?
Got any change? A customer tipped me a coat button and asked for a receipt.
It's a lovely button. I still have rent, though.
Can you hear that squeak? New boots. Everyone hears me coming.
I did our stock count by candlelight. It says we need fourteen tins of soup and one tin of soap.
I'm fairly sure the cook meant soup. Fairly sure isn't enough. I'll take both.
Can I have the dented tin? I'll be opening it in ten minutes anyway.
A regular came in, paid for an hour and asked if we could just sit in silence.
Quietest money I ever made. Best hour of my week, too.
Is your fridge humming in B flat? Ours does. I hear it in my sleep.
My gran's Dutch soup recipe says to add a handful of onions. You never met my gran. Her hands were enormous.
Better give me another onion. I'd like this to taste like home.
Can I keep the soup hot here for a minute? My sister's just across the quay.
A customer took both our umbrellas by mistake. Came back with three.
I put them behind the desk. At this rate we'll be selling them by winter.
Anything small enough for this pocket? The other one's full of keys.
Three encores in heels. People call it talent. My toes have a different word for it.
I gave the bouquet to the lighting tech. He's the one who found my heel in the dark.
Could you tie the parcel? My nails are still wet.
A client swears he's fine and now half the night's gossip is about Brindle Fever.
Everybody's a doctor till somebody asks them what time the clinic opens.
I've had enough advice tonight. A sealed drink and something to eat will do until I get seen.
The sign says open. Please tell me that includes the till.
Had a client ask if my real name came with the hour. My dear, the tailor who lets out these cuffs has only just earned it.
He laughed. We played cards. Turns out he's been introducing himself with a made-up name, too.
Got a spare minute? I want to finish this drink while it's cold.
You remember a tune differently after you sing it to an empty room.
The cleaner clapped. She said I shouldn't have to pack my own applause away with the mic.
Honey for my tea if you've got it. We're rehearsing the quiet songs.
I went in to ask for a raise. Came out with three people's rota changes and a broken stapler.
I'm going back after lunch. Would you mind writing 'raise' on the bag?
A sandwich I can eat one-handed. The other hand's keeping this paperwork together.
Somebody left an engagement ring in the cloakroom. Three people have described it perfectly.
I'm asking them what coat it was in. Funny how nobody remembers the coat.
Have you seen a coat ticket with a little heart on it? Worth more than my lunch today.
I took the long way round. They painted over the height marks on my old doorframe.
My brother cheated on the top one. Stood on a book. I'd quite like that silly mark back.
I'll take the smaller tin. It fits beside my brother's things.
We hung a sign saying the house cat isn't staff. First person in asked for the cat by name.
I suppose she has regulars. Still hasn't covered a shift for me.
Fish for the cat, something cheaper for me. Don't look at me like that.
Someone requested a love song and spent all three verses reading a repair invoice.
At the end he kissed the paper. Apparently Joe Wild had knocked a zero off.
Something for the drummer. He's been paid entirely in applause again.
I'm holding a table for two people who haven't spoken in eight years.
Set it for four. Their elbows need somewhere to go while they figure out what to say.
A small box of tea. I can always find two cups.
I tried telling a joke between numbers. The speaker cut out right before the punch line.
Biggest laugh I've ever had. I'm taking the sound man to dinner.
Got something for two? One of us owes the other a laugh.
I had my eyelids painted gold this evening. It took an hour. I fell asleep before anyone saw them.
The others let me sleep. Kept saying my act was very modern.
Anything for breakfast? I've slept straight through dinner.
I promised a new starter I'd wait until their tram arrived. We watched three go by.
Fourth one was nearly empty. That was the one they could face. Home now, thank goodness.
Two waters. I don't like sending anyone to the stop empty-handed.
My father never liked my stage name. He used it on a letter for the first time today.
I'm going to frame the envelope. The letter's mostly about his drain.
Have a dry bag? There's a letter in my pocket I can't let get wet.
One of our lads turned a booking down. The client wanted his money back and an apology from the lad himself.
I counted out his change. He can book an hour here. He can't buy a yes.
Something to share at the rota meeting. Sweet if it's bad news.
Someone asked if the flower in my hair was for sale. I said it was my uniform.
He offered to buy my uniform. So I sold him an apron from lost property.
Is there a mirror behind the till? My braid caught on the tram door.
I need a tin with a lid that fits. Last night the cook and I sorted thirty lids and found one pair.
We stood there clapping like we'd just delivered a baby.
Two identical tins. I am begging you, identical.
I save the last dance for the people stacking the chairs. Nobody asks them for one.
Last night the dishwasher swept me clean off my feet. Best shoes in the building.
A cold drink for the dishwasher. He's earned it.
My braid caught a sequin curtain as I walked out. Half the stage set followed me down the quay.
I picked up every piece. If it sparkles in your doorway, that's the last one.
Has glitter got into the till? Entirely possible that's my fault.
Dr. Jackson keeps a clipboard by the counter. I tried doing that at work.
Within a night somebody had booked the clipboard itself for two private dances.
Dinner to go. Apparently even office supplies get a break before I do.
Someone called me brave for working nights. I said my mum worked mornings at the docks.
Try waking her at four. That's brave.
I'll take two rolls. Mum eats the crusty one on the walk in.
A client complained the room was too dark. He was still wearing his sunglasses.
I let him discover it himself. Takes restraint. Put that on my payslip.
Just water. I've done enough smiling for tips tonight.
One of the new girls called in sick and said sorry six times. I used to make that call from this very corner.
I told her the rota's my problem. A person ought to get ill without doing sums.
Soup that reheats well, please. I'm leaving it by a friend's door.
I used to think the hard part was singing the high note. It's remembering who's missing from the front row.
Tonight somebody sat in his chair. I got all the way through.
Plain water. The first note tomorrow needs to be mine.
I'm collecting for an emergency cab fund. One credit each, whenever there's a good night.
Last week it got a porter home to see his baby before she fell asleep. Worth the jar space.
Can you break a ten? The little coins are for a fare home.
A woman asked me to wake her before closing. Didn't want company. She wanted one safe hour of sleep.
I sat by the door and kept the music down. She tipped me with a peppermint.
Something minty for the reception desk. I want to pass one on.
The delivery slip says six cases. We got six individual lemons wearing paper hats.
They're lovely hats. Still five cases and a bit short.
How many on a full tray? I count everything twice these days.
I spent an hour listening to a regular rehearse a breakup. Then he rang his landlord.
Turns out the great love of his life was a flat with working heat.
A hot meal, if you have one. My own flat isn't exactly a love story.
I found an old cassette with my first set on it. My voice shakes so badly you can hear my earring hit the mic.
I've kept it. Some nights I forget how hard it was just to stand there.
Something for the walk home. I've got a tape to listen to.
I use a little star next to quiet bookings. Last night one of the regulars drew one beside my name.
Nobody disturbed my break. I want to do that for somebody else.
A meal for the desk. Today I'm taking the whole break.
First night at the window in a new suit. A client said I looked just like his ex-husband.
I've met his ex-husband. I'm keeping the suit.
Need a drink that won't stain a white cuff. Trust me on this.
I know the posters say to see Dr. Jackson. I know where his desk is. I'd go now if the clinic were open.
What I can do tonight is buy a drink, sit still for a bit, and stop pretending I'm fine.
A little water for the tram, please. It's a long way home when you're tired.
We ran out of dressing-room hooks. I spent half my shift introducing coats to chairs like guests at a wedding.
Your velvet sleeve, madam, has been seated beside the till.
Anything hot left? I finally got a chair of my own.
I sang a birthday song for a man who'd come in on his own. Quiet little thing.
He said it was the first time anyone got his name right. I wrote it on next year's calendar.
One sweet thing for a birthday, please. I'll sort the candle.
I sign the night crew out in pairs. One of them wrote me in on the last line tonight.
It didn't occur to me anyone was counting me, too.
Two drinks with lids. We're catching the same tram.
Someone asked what a man like me was doing with a flower in his hair. I said, 'Keeping it watered.'
He bought me a glass of water. That might be the best tip I've ever earned.
Bunch of flowers costs more than lunch. Today I'm having lunch.
I bring food back in everyone's order of hunger. The new cook keeps putting himself last.
Tonight I'm writing his name on the first bowl. With a marker. Let them argue with that.
Something filling that travels well. I've got people waiting.
